chunks: 4288 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

“I hold that one should not swear except by Allah. As for a man’s saying, ‘No, by your enemy,’ then indeed that is from the speech of al-Jahiliyyah. And if people were to swear by this or the like of it, swearing by Allah would be abandoned. As for a man’s saying, ‘Yā Hanāh, Yā Hanāh,’ that is only seeking the name, and I do not see any harm in it. And as for ‘Laʿamru Allah’ and ‘Aymu Allah,’ that is indeed by Allah.”

key_terms.أَيْمُ اللَّهِ: an oath formula meaning by the oath of Allah
key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: the pre-Islamic age of ignorance and its ways
key_terms.بِاللَّهِ: by Allah; the proper object of oath in this context
key_terms.شَانِئِكَ: your enemy; used here in a condemned oath expression
key_terms.طَلَبُ الِاسْمِ: calling or seeking the name; merely naming someone
key_terms.لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ: an oath formula meaning by the life of Allah
key_terms.يُحْلَفَ: to swear or take an oath

ai.seo_question: What kinds of oath expressions are permissible, and should one swear only by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that oaths should be made only by Allah and rejects expressions rooted in al-Jahiliyyah. It also distinguishes between objectionable oath formulas and harmless expressions that merely call out a name, while affirming that phrases such as «لَعَمْرُ اللَّهِ» and «أَيْمُ اللَّهِ» count as swearing by Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4288 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said:

"I believe that one should only swear by Allah (swt).
As for a man's saying, 'No, by your enemy,' this is from the sayings of Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic era of ignorance). If people were to swear by this or similar expressions, swearing by Allah (swt) would be abandoned.
As for a man's saying, 'Ya Hanah, Ya Hanah' (O so-and-so), it is merely calling a name, and I see no harm in it.
And as for saying, 'By the life of Allah (swt)' (La 'amr Allah (swt)) and 'By the oath of Allah (swt)' (Aym Allah (swt)), these are indeed swearing by Allah (swt)."
